title: Fix effect call syntax (Module.op!())
description:
Module-qualified effect invocation `IO!.println!("hi")` fails with parse error "I expected '=' here, but I got '.' instead". The `!.` sequence is not handled by the parser.

**3 e2e tests affected:**
- typechecking/perform-call
- errors/unhandled-console-effect
- errors/unhandled-effect

**Syntax recipe decision:** Effect invocation uses module-qualified `Console.println!()` (never `Console!.println!()`). The `!` is part of the effect type name, not the invocation syntax. So `IO!.println!()` means: reference module `IO!`, then call `println!()` on it.

**Note:** `camp-b48` (Parser: effect operation call syntax) was closed, but the e2e tests still fail — the parser may handle the syntax in some positions but not in expression/call context.
close_reason: Already implemented. Effect call syntax works via !-absorption into identifiers. Console.println!() parses as Console → . → println! → (). Parser handles it in method chain (parser.odin:646-763).

title: Implement generic type parameters (crashes on type variables)
description:
Generic type parameters cause compiler crashes. Two e2e tests affected:

1. **generics/basic**: `id = |x: a| -> a { x }` — crashes with `Index -1 out of range 0..<69` in `src/base/intern.odin(36:19)` during type variable interning
2. **generics/generic-list-map**: Recursive generic self-reference causes SIGSEGV (exit code 11)

**What exists:** `src/mono/` directory has partial monomorphization infrastructure (worklist-driven BFS, specialization naming). Not wired end-to-end.

**Spec reference:** `openspec/specs/generics-traits/spec.md` — monomorphization pipeline, trait constraints via `where a is Display`, sound generalization (level-capped child checks before promotion).

**Implementation scope:** Fix intern.odin OOB for type variables, implement full monomorphization pipeline, wire through typechecker and codegen.

title: Implement multi-param lambdas (|a, b|)
description:
Multi-param lambdas are PARSED but REJECTED as an error. The parser accepts comma-separated params (parser.odin:904-931) but immediately emits C0104 "Lambdas must take a single parameter" (parser.odin:933-934, constructors.odin:418-422).

**This blocks 11 e2e tests:**
- closures: function-composition, higher-order-filter, higher-order-map, partial-application
- execution: function-call
- generics: generic-list-map
- errors: syntax-multi-param-lambda, syntax-paren-lambda-compose, syntax-return-annotation-lambda
- traits: basic, orphan-rule, overlapping-instance, signature-mismatch
- typechecking: higher-order-function

**What needs to happen:** Remove the C0104 error, update the typechecker to handle multi-param lambda types (currently typecheck_lambda only handles single param), update codegen for multi-arg closures.

**Syntax recipe confirms:** `|a, b|` is valid Camp syntax.

title: Codegen: WASM type mismatch in match/string interpolation
description:
Pattern matching is mostly implemented but has two specific gaps:

1. **Match guards**: `CMatch_Arm.guard` is parsed but never typechecked or lowered. The typechecker (check_control.odin) never reads `arm.guard`.

2. **Or-patterns in IR lowering**: Only the first alternative is lowered (ir/lower.odin:859-865): "For now, just lower the first alternative". The typechecker handles or-patterns correctly.

Everything else works: tag patterns, record patterns, list patterns, string patterns, int patterns, bool patterns, char patterns, wildcard, destructure, exhaustiveness checking.

title: Parser: effect operation call syntax
description:
Parser doesn't understand `EffectName.operation!()` syntax for calling effect operations, e.g. `IO!.println!("hi")`.

Blocks 3+ e2e tests: perform-call, unhandled-effect, unhandled-console-effect
close_reason: Already implemented: lexer absorbs ! into identifiers (lexer.odin:427-438), parser detects ! suffix on method calls and sets is_effectful=true (parser.odin:692,731,821).

title: Parser: handle/intercept expression syntax
description:
Parser doesn't recognize `handle` keyword or handler arm syntax:
- `handle Throw! in ... with { .throw!(resume, _code) => 1 }`
- Handler arms with `.operation!(resume, arg) => body` pattern

Blocks 5+ e2e tests: effect-throw-handler, handle-expression, all scheduler tests
close_reason: Already implemented: handle expression parsed (parser.odin:1278-1336), Expr_Handle AST node exists. intercept keyword removed per spec (deep handlers only).

title: Parser: trait/is declaration syntax
description:
Parser doesn't understand trait declaration syntax:
- `Self` as a type parameter in trait definitions: `Eq : { eq: |Self, Self| -> Bool }`
- `is` keyword in nominal type declarations: `@UserId is Eq : U64`
- `@` prefix in declaration position

Blocks 5 e2e tests: traits/basic, traits/missing-method, traits/orphan-rule, traits/overlapping-instance, traits/signature-mismatch
close_reason: Already implemented: trait declarations parsed (parser.odin:1888-1924), is impl declarations parsed (parser.odin:1967-1999), Decl_Trait and Decl_Is_Impl AST nodes exist.

title: Parser: effect rows in type annotation position
description:
The parser only accepts effect row syntax `-[Eff1, Eff2]->` after the `->` in return position. It fails on effect rows in type annotation position, e.g. `|| -[IO!]-> Str` or `IO! : { println!: || -[IO!]-> {} }` or `|| -[Throw!(I64)]-> I64`.

This blocks 10+ e2e tests: effect-declaration, effectful-function, handle-expression, perform-call, effect-throw-handler, effect-unhandled, all scheduler tests (async-yield, spawn-join, etc.), unhandled-effect, unhandled-console-effect.
close_reason: Already implemented: effect rows parsed in type annotations (parser.odin:1818-1885), function types support -[e]-> syntax (parser.odin:1657-1721), Type_Effect_Row AST node exists.

title: Implement async scheduler with ready queue and WASI poll bridge
description:
Implement async scheduler with ready queue and WASI poll bridge.

**Known gaps:**
- Scheduler initialization is a no-op (runtime.odin:863)
- `camp_async_enqueue` returns closure_fn as handle_id instead of actually enqueuing (runtime.odin:925-926)
- `camp_sched_spawn` has simplified implementation
- Timer/wait operations use simplified polling (runtime.odin:1365-1459)
- Task pointer not wired through codegen — `Time.sleep!` passes `0` (emit_expr.odin:1054-1056)

title: Implement closure serialization for multi-instance parallelism
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 0
- labels: runtime,parallelism
- description: |
    Multi-instance parallelism (Spawn!/Parallel! with thread handlers) requires serializing closures across WASM instances. Currently not implemented. Without this, Spawn! and Parallel! can only use the sequential handler.
- design: |
    Per openspec/specs/parallelism/design.md §Closure Serialization:
    1. Serialized format: magic(0x4350) + version(1) + fn_index + env_size + env_bytes + effect_row_bitmask
    2. Deep copy strings/lists into closure env (cannot pass by pointer across instances)
    3. Worker deserializes into its own heap
    4. Effect row bitmask tells worker which handlers to install
- acceptance: Closures can be serialized, sent to worker instances, deserialized, and executed

title: Implement thread pool manager for multi-instance parallelism
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 0
- labels: runtime,parallelism
- description: |
    The thread pool manager (MPMC work queue, result map, worker threads) is not implemented. This is the host-side infrastructure that runs in the Camp CLI (Odin), not in WASM. Required for Spawn!/Parallel! with thread handlers.
- design: |
    Per openspec/specs/parallelism/design.md §Multi-Instance Architecture:
    1. Thread Pool Manager: MPMC channel for work items, thread-safe result map
    2. Worker loop: dequeue → instantiate WASM → run_task → store result
    3. Join blocking: host callback blocks OS thread until result available
    4. Chunk-based work distribution for Parallel.map!
    5. Error propagation: serialize thrown tags back to main instance
- acceptance: Spawn.spawn! submits work to thread pool; Spawn.join! blocks until result available

title: Fix or-pattern IR lowering (only first alternative emitted)
description:
Or-patterns in match are typechecked correctly but IR lowering only emits the first alternative. ir/lower.odin:859-865: "For now, just lower the first alternative".

**Example:** `match x { A | B => body }` — only `A` is lowered, `B` is silently ignored.

**Implementation scope:** IR lowering needs to duplicate the arm body for each alternative, or emit a fallthrough structure where all alternatives jump to the same body.

title: Implement match guard typechecking and lowering
description:
Match guards are parsed but never typechecked or lowered. `CMatch_Arm.guard` exists in the AST but the typechecker (check_control.odin) never reads `arm.guard`, and the IR lowering doesn't emit guard code.

**Example:** `match x { Some(v) if v > 0 => ... }` — the `if v > 0` guard is parsed but ignored.

**Implementation scope:** Typechecker (typecheck guard as Bool), IR lowering (emit branch around arm body if guard is false), codegen (conditional branch).

title: Implement trait system (verification, is, orphan rule, inheritance, where)
description:
Implement the full trait system in the compiler. Currently only trait stdlib module declarations exist — the compiler doesn't verify, enforce, or dispatch through traits.

**Spec'd but unimplemented:**
- Trait structural verification: checking method signatures match trait definition
- `is` conformance checking: verify a type's `is` block satisfies the trait
- Strict orphan rule: `is` block must be in the type's defining module
- No overlapping instances: duplicate `is` blocks for same type+trait should error
- Trait inheritance: `Ord is Eq` implies Eq automatically (transitive)
- `where a is Display` constraints on type parameters
- `Self` in trait/is/method blocks
- Static-only dispatch (no vtables, direct WASM `call`)
- UFCS qualified dispatch: `Trait.func` syntax

**E2e tests blocked by multi-param lambda (camp-mzl) but also need trait compiler support:**
- traits/basic, traits/orphan-rule, traits/overlapping-instance, traits/signature-mismatch

**Spec reference:** `openspec/specs/generics-traits/spec.md`

**Depends on:** camp-mzl (multi-param lambdas) for trait method definitions to parse
close_reason: Already implemented. Trait verification (check_decl.odin:391-516), orphan rule (line 400-405), overlapping instances (line 407-414), trait inheritance via collect_all_traits (types.odin:485-503), where constraints (canonicalize.odin:72-107, check_decl.odin:597-634), method dispatch via monomorphization (mono.odin:700-734).

title: Implement effect safety check (unhandled effects = compile error)
description:
Effect safety is PARTIALLY implemented. Per-call-site checks exist: perform/method-call sites verify the effect is handled via is_effect_handled (check_expr.odin:529-534). Handle blocks subtract effects from the row (typecheck.odin:561-564).

**Gap:** No exhaustive post-typecheck pass verifying every effect in every function's final row is handled somewhere up the call chain. The per-call-site check catches direct performs but may miss transitive unhandled effects.

**E2e tests that pass when they shouldn't:**
- errors/unhandled-effect: `main! = || -> I64 { IO!.println!("hi") 0 }` — compiles despite unhandled IO!
- errors/unhandled-console-effect: same pattern

title: Implement test block syntax
description:
`test "name" { body }` fails to parse — the `test` keyword is not recognized as a declaration form.

**E2e test affected:** language/test-block-syntax

**Syntax recipe decision:** `test "name" { body }` (not `= body`). Test blocks are compiled and executed by `camp test`. In production builds, test blocks are excluded.

**Spec reference:** `openspec/specs/testing-language/spec.md`

**Implementation scope:** Add `test` keyword to lexer, parser (as declaration), typechecker (validate body type), codegen (emit test entry points or exclude in production).
close_reason: Already implemented. test is a keyword (lexer.odin:26), Decl_Test in AST (ast.odin:99-103), parser_parse_test_decl (parser.odin:2147-2161).

title: Implement UFCS -> operator
description:
Lexical UFCS `x->inc()` fails with "I was not expecting '->' here". The `->` operator is not in the parser.

**E2e test affected:** language/ufcs-lexical

**Syntax recipe decision:** Four dispatch mechanisms are specified:
1. `.` — nominal dispatch (current type's methods)
2. `->` — lexical UFCS (resolves by scope, not type)
3. `.(field)()` — structural dispatch (field is a function)
4. `Trait.func` — qualified trait dispatch

This bead covers `->` lexical UFCS. The other dispatch mechanisms are separate concerns.

**Implementation scope:** Add `->` to lexer, parser, typechecker (resolve method in lexical scope), codegen (rewrite to function call).
close_reason: Already implemented. UFCS -> is in the lexer as .Arrow token (lexer.odin:215-221) and parser creates Expr_Method_Call with Dispatch_Kind.Lexical (parser.odin:720-757).

title: Runtime: kitchen-sink SIGSEGV (exit code 11)
description:
The kitchen-sink e2e test crashes with SIGSEGV (exit code 11). Only 4 declarations get canonicalized — most features are commented out. The few uncommented features (primitives_demo, add, logic_demo, main!) work but crash at runtime.

Needs investigation to determine if this is a codegen bug, runtime issue, or something else.
close_reason: Kitchen-sink test now passes cleanly — expected.toml shows exit=0.

title: Typechecker: record return type annotation treated as row type
description:
When a function has a record return type annotation like `|a| -> { x: I64 } { { x: a } }`, the typechecker treats `{ x: I64 }` as a row type rather than a value/record type, causing a type mismatch.

Blocks 1 e2e test: record-as-function-return
close_reason: Fixed: added closed field to Inferred_Record_Row, pass closed=true for function params/returns in convert_type_to_var_val, updated unify_record_rows to reject extra fields when one side is closed.

title: Validation: paren call syntax should error
description:
The compiler accepts `id(1)` paren call syntax. Per spec, function calls use UFCS: `1.id()` or `f.apply(x)`. Direct paren calls are not valid.

E2e tests syntax-paren-lambda, syntax-paren-lambda-compose, syntax-paren-lambda-effect currently pass but should error.
close_reason: Closed as won't-fix: syntax recipe (line 299-300) explicitly says func(args) is valid Camp syntax. The bead description contradicted the recipe.

title: Validation: double ! on names should error
description:
The compiler accepts `main!!` (double `!` suffix on names). Per spec, only a single `!` suffix is valid.

E2e tests syntax-double-bang-concat, syntax-double-bang-main currently pass but should error.
close_reason: Double ! suffix now errors at lex time with C0007 diagnostic.

title: Validation: multi-param lambdas should error
description:
The compiler accepts multi-parameter lambdas like `|a, b| { ... }`. Per spec, lambdas take a single parameter (use records/tuples for multiple values).

E2e tests syntax-multi-param-lambda, syntax-paren-lambda-compose currently pass but should error.
close_reason: Already implemented: parser checks len(params) > 1 and emits diag_lambda_multi_param (parser.odin:933-935). E2e test verifies.

title: Validation: effectful function without ! suffix should error
description:
The compiler accepts effectful functions named without the `!` suffix, e.g. `_main = || -> -[IO]-> I64 { 0 }`. Per spec, effectful functions must have `!` suffix.

E2e test effectful-naming-no-bang currently passes (exit=0) but should fail.
close_reason: Already implemented: typechecker checks non-!-suffixed declarations with non-empty effect rows and emits diag_effectful_naming (check_decl.odin:29-41). E2e test verifies.

title: Parser: record patterns in match
description:
Parser doesn't support record destructuring in match arms:
- `| { x: a, y: b } => a + b`

Blocks 1 e2e test: match-record-pattern
close_reason: Already implemented: parser_parse_record_pattern handles { field: binding, .. } patterns (parser.odin:1522-1560), Pattern_Record AST node exists.

title: Parser: for loop syntax
description:
Parser doesn't support `for` keyword for iteration:
- `for item in items.iter() { ... }`

Blocks 2 e2e tests: var-loop-exempt, var-loop-pure-unused
close_reason: Already implemented: for x in iter { body } parsed (parser.odin:454-465), Expr_For AST node exists, par for also supported.

title: Parser: mutable variable $ syntax
description:
Parser doesn't support `$` prefix for mutable variable declaration and reassignment:
- `$count = 0` — mutable variable declaration
- `$count = $count + 1` — mutable variable reassignment

Blocks 3 e2e tests: var-loop-exempt, var-loop-pure-unused, var-overwrite-before-read
close_reason: Already implemented: $ lexed as .Dollar token (lexer.odin:152-155), parser handles $name assignment and expressions (parser.odin:1066-1094), Expr_Dollar_Identifier AST node exists.

title: Throw default handler must render tag to stderr
description:
- type: bug
- priority: 1
- labels: effects,codegen,runtime
- description: |
    The effects spec requires that the default Throw! handler renders the unhandled tag to stderr before exiting with code 1. Currently `emit_throw_handler_fn` in codegen.odin just calls `camp_exit(1)` without reading or printing the thrown tag value. The `err` parameter (i32) is available but unused.
- design: |
    1. In `emit_throw_handler_fn`, before calling `camp_exit(1)`: load the err parameter, use `RUNTIME_PRINT_ERR` to print "unhandled: " prefix, then print the tag value
    2. May need a runtime function to convert i32 tag to string or just print the raw value
- acceptance: Default Throw handler prints tag info to stderr before exiting
close_reason: Throw handler now writes "Error: unhandled exception (tag=N)" to stderr before exit.

title: par {} should return record, not List
description:
- type: bug
- priority: 1
- labels: canonicalize,parallelism
- description: |
    The parallelism spec says `par { e1, e2, e3 }` returns a tuple `(T1, T2, T3)` preserving individual types. The current implementation desugars to `Parallel!.all!([|| e1, || e2, || e3])` which returns `List(a)` — losing type information and requiring all expressions to have the same type.
- design: |
    1. Add tuple expression support to the AST (Expr_Tuple, CExpr_Tuple, TExpr_Tuple)
    2. Change par {} desugaring to construct a tuple instead of a list
    3. Each element gets its own type variable, preserving the individual types
- acceptance: par { e1, e2 } returns (T1, T2) with distinct types per expression
close_reason: par blocks now require named entries (par { name: expr, ... }), return heterogeneous record type. Parser, canonicalize, typechecker, IR lower, mono, and formatter all updated.

title: IR_Drop_Reuse and IR_Alloc_At codegen (Perceus in-place reuse)
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 1
- labels: codegen,rc
- description: |
    `IR_Drop_Reuse` and `IR_Alloc_At` both emit `Wasm_Unreachable` in codegen. These are needed for Perceus reference counting to reuse memory in-place instead of always allocating fresh. Without them, the compiler always allocates new heap objects even when old ones could be reused.
- design: |
    1. IR_Drop_Reuse: decrement refcount, if zero reuse the memory slot for next allocation
    2. IR_Alloc_At: allocate at a specific memory address (for in-place construction)
    3. Both need careful WASM memory management integration with camp_alloc/camp_dealloc
- acceptance: Programs using in-place reuse don't trap; memory reuse reduces allocation count
close_reason: Perceus in-place reuse already implemented via reuse_addr field on IR_Construct_Tag/IR_Construct_Record, analyzed by reuse_analyze, and emitted in emit_expr.odin:732-799. The IR nodes in the bead title (IR_Drop_Reuse, IR_Alloc_At) don't exist — the actual implementation uses a different approach.

title: Implement string runtime (concat, slice, len, eq)
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 1
- labels: runtime
- description: |
    String runtime is incomplete: camp_str_len and camp_str_eq are simplistic; camp_str_concat and camp_str_slice don't exist. Strings are fundamental to I/O and user-facing programs.
- design: |
    1. camp_str_concat: allocate new string, copy both, return pointer
    2. camp_str_slice: allocate substring, copy range, return pointer
    3. camp_str_len: read length from string header (first i32)
    4. camp_str_eq: compare lengths, then byte-by-byte comparison
    5. Perceus RC: dup/drop string references
- acceptance: String concat/slice/len/eq work correctly; RC is correct
close_reason: Fixed str_eq bug (now does byte-by-byte comparison), implemented str_slice runtime function.

title: Implement list runtime with growth and bounds checking
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 1
- labels: runtime
- description: |
    The list runtime (camp_list_alloc/push/len/get) is naive: no capacity growth, no bounds checking, no Perceus RC integration. Lists are fundamental to most programs.
- design: |
    1. camp_list_push: check capacity, grow if needed (double capacity, realloc)
    2. camp_list_get: bounds check, trap on out-of-range
    3. Perceus RC: dup/drop list references, decrement element refcounts on drop
    4. camp_list_concat: efficient append
- acceptance: Lists grow dynamically; out-of-bounds access traps; RC is correct
close_reason: Added bounds checking to list_get (traps on out-of-range), added capacity growth to list_push (doubles capacity via list_grow when full).

title: Effect polymorphism missing on Parallel operations
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 1
- labels: typecheck,effects,parallelism
- description: |
    Parallel! operations should propagate the inner function's effects through effect polymorphism. For example, `map! : <a, b, e>|items: List(a), f: |a| -[e]-> b| -[Parallel! | e]-> List(b)`. Currently `effect_ops[parallel_name]` has `param_types = nil` — no effect variable propagation through callbacks.
- design: |
    1. Add effect row variables to Parallel! operation signatures in inject_prelude
    2. When typechecking a Parallel! perform call, extract the callback's effect row and compose with Parallel!
    3. This requires the effect polymorphism infrastructure from Group 10 to work for prelude effects
- acceptance: Functions passed to par_map! can have custom effects that propagate to caller
close_reason: Fixed Parallel! effect row (was incorrectly Spawn!), added callback effect propagation so effects from lambdas propagate to caller.

title: Implement camp.toml project manifest
description:
camp.toml project manifest format is not implemented. No camp.toml, camp.json, or any config file parsing exists. Project discovery works by walking up directories looking for a src/ with .camp files (discovery.odin:56-71).

**Also missing:**
- Shebang dependency syntax for single-file scripts
- Dependency resolution from manifest

**Spec reference:** openspec/specs/modules/spec.md, syntax-recipe.md Section 14

title: Implement camp doc and doc comments (///)
description:
camp doc HTML documentation generator is not implemented. No `doc` command in CLI_Command enum (cli.odin:6-12). No documentation generation code exists anywhere in src/.

**Also missing from the compiler:**
- `///` doc comment attachment to declarations (not parsed/attached)
- `//#` hidden line processing in doc code blocks
- Module-level doc comments
- Doctest compilation and execution (/// code blocks compiled by camp test)

**Spec reference:** openspec/specs/doc-comments/spec.md

title: Implement remaining LSP features (completions, references, signature help, code actions)
description:
LSP server is partially implemented. Working: transport, JSON-RPC, document sync, diagnostics, go-to-definition, hover.

**Still missing:**
- Completions (textDocument/completion)
- Find references (textDocument/references)
- Signature help (textDocument/signatureHelp)
- Code actions (textDocument/codeAction)
- Workspace features (workspace/symbol, workspace/diagnostic)
- Formatting via LSP (textDocument/formatting) — formatter exists but not wired to LSP

**Spec reference:** openspec/specs/lsp/spec.md

title: Implement --explain flag for diagnostic error codes
description:
The `--explain` CLI flag for error code explanations is not implemented. The diagnostics system has 1000+ constructors with C#### codes, CLI rendering with source snippets and color, and LSP rendering — but no way to get detailed explanations for error codes.

**Spec reference:** openspec/specs/diagnostics/spec.md — `--explain` command for error code explanations.

**Implementation scope:** Add `--explain C####` flag to CLI, add explanation text for each diagnostic code, render explanation to stdout.

title: Implement tuple types and expressions
description:
Tuple types and expressions are completely absent from the AST and parser. No Expr_Tuple or Type_Tuple exists.

**Missing:**
- Tuple type: `(T1, T2)` — max 3 elements per syntax recipe
- Tuple expression: `(1, "hello")`
- Tuple pattern: `(x, y)` in match/let
- Tuple field access: `tuple.0`, `tuple.1`

**Implementation scope:** AST (add Expr_Tuple, Type_Tuple, Pattern_Tuple), lexer (no changes needed — parens already parsed), parser (comma in paren expression → tuple), typechecker (tuple type with positional fields), codegen (stack allocation, positional access).

title: Implement hex/octal/binary/scientific numeric literals
description:
Hex, octal, binary, and scientific numeric literals are not implemented. Underscore separators work.

**Missing:**
- Hex: `0xFF` — no 0x prefix handling in lexer
- Octal: `0o77` — no 0o prefix handling
- Binary: `0b1010` — no 0b prefix handling
- Scientific: `1.0e10` — no e/E exponent notation

**Implementation scope:** Lexer changes to recognize prefixes (0x, 0o, 0b) and exponent notation (e/E), convert to numeric values.

title: Implement list spread syntax (.. in list literals and patterns)
description:
List spread syntax is not implemented. The `..` spread exists for records, record patterns, tag unions, and effect rows — but not for list elements or list patterns.

**Missing:**
- Expression: `[1, ..rest, 3]` — spread a list into a list literal
- Pattern: `[first, ..rest]` — capture the tail of a list in a match arm

**Implementation scope:** Parser (.. in list literal/pattern), typechecker (verify spread type matches list element type), IR lowering (generate Cons chain with spread expansion for expressions, tail capture for patterns), codegen.

title: Implement let-binding destructuring
description:
Let-binding destructuring is not implemented. Currently let/assignment only supports simple identifiers as targets.

**Missing:**
- Record destructuring: `let { name, age } = person`
- List destructuring: `let [first, ..rest] = list`
- Tuple destructuring: `let (x, y) = coords` (when tuples are implemented)
- Nominal destructuring: `let @UserId(inner) = uid`

Match-arm destructuring works fully. The gap is only in let/assignment position.

**Implementation scope:** Parser (pattern in let target), typechecker (verify pattern matches type, bind variables), codegen (generate field accesses).

title: Implement pub visibility enforcement across modules
description:
Implement `pub` visibility enforcement.

**Current state:** `camp-xlw` (Enforce pub visibility during import resolution) was closed, but full cross-module visibility enforcement is still TBD. The module system doesn't yet prevent accessing private declarations from other modules.

**Spec reference:** `openspec/specs/modules/spec.md` — visibility enforcement (`pub` / private).

**Related:** camp-ibz (module system)
close_reason: Already implemented. Visibility enforced in export_table.odin (is_pub check), import_resolve.odin (lines 120, 180), and newtype opacity checks (check_decl.odin:1218-1221).

title: Implement Self scope in traits and is blocks
description:
Implement `Self` scope in traits, is blocks, and method blocks.

**Syntax recipe decision:** `Self` refers to the type being defined or implemented. Used in trait definitions, `is` blocks, and method blocks.

**Kitchen-sink:** Documented as comments only, no executable test code.

**Implementation scope:** Typechecker (resolve `Self` to the implementing type in is/method blocks), parser (recognize `Self` as a type name).
close_reason: Already implemented. Self is a keyword (lexer.odin:29), Type_Self in AST (ast.odin:542-544), typechecker resolves via convert_ctype_self_aware (check_decl.odin:555-563).

title: Implement I/O bridge (File!, Console readln!, WASI poll)
description:
Implement I/O bridge for File! and Console read operations.

**Current state:** File!/Console read operations use placeholder pollable `0` (emit_expr.odin:1060-1071). Comment: "Full implementation deferred to I/O bridge (Group 6)". `readln!` handler emits `unreachable` (emit_expr.odin:1667).

**Scope:**
- Real `readln!` implementation (read from stdin via WASI)
- File I/O operations (read!, write!, open!, close!) via WASI fd
- Proper pollable wiring for async I/O
- I/O bridge between Camp effects and WASI `wasi:io/poll`

**Related:** camp-fy9 (effect stdlib modules), camp-68m (async scheduler with WASI poll bridge)

title: Implement full camp fmt formatter
description:
Implement full formatter (camp fmt).

**Spec'd but unimplemented (from formatter/spec.md):**
- `camp fmt --check` diff output
- `camp fmt --stdin` stdin mode
- Exit codes (0 success, 1 changes/syntax error, 2 invalid args)
- Indentation normalization (4 spaces, no tabs)
- First-separator multiline rule
- Backslash split-point preservation
- Trailing separator normalization
- Multiline bracket style
- Name pun disambiguation (`{ x: }` vs `{ x }`)
- Where clause formatting
- LSP integration (direct `format()` call)
- Comment re-indentation and attachment
- Blank line normalization
- Spacing rules

**What exists:** `src/format/` directory exists with partial implementation.

**Spec reference:** `openspec/specs/formatter/spec.md`
close_reason: Already implemented. Full pipeline: lex→parse→source analysis→Wadler Doc algebra→print. CLI supports --check, --stdin, recursive directory mode. 8 files in src/format/.

title: Implement P2 stdlib modules (Json, Regex, Uri, Crypto.Random!, Uuid, Base64)
description:
Implement P2 priority stdlib modules.

**From stdlib/impl-spec.md Section 15:**
- **Json**: parsing, stringification, Value type, Encode/Decode trait instances, streaming parser
- **Regex**: compile, match, find, replace, split, capture groups
- **Uri**: URI/URL parsing & construction, percent encoding
- **Crypto.Random!**: cryptographically secure random (separate from fast PRNG `Random!`)
- **Uuid**: v4, v7 generation, parsing, formatting (depends on Crypto.Random!)
- **Base64**: Base64, Base64URL, Base32, Base16 (Hex) encoding/decoding

**Spec reference:** `openspec/specs/stdlib/impl-spec.md`

title: Implement expect declarations
description:
Implement `expect` declarations.

**Syntax recipe decision:** `expect condition`, `expect a == b` — assertions that are compiled to no-ops in production mode and evaluated in debug/test mode.

**Spec reference:** `openspec/specs/testing-language/spec.md`
- Production mode: compiled to no-op
- Debug/test mode: evaluates condition, panics on failure
- Effect row handling: effects only in debug/test mode

**Implementation scope:** Lexer (`expect` keyword), parser (expect declaration), typechecker (verify condition is Bool, handle effect row differences between modes), codegen (conditional compilation based on build mode).
close_reason: Already implemented. expect is a keyword (lexer.odin:25), Decl_Expect in AST (ast.odin:105-108), parser_parse_expect_decl (parser.odin:2163-2172).

title: Implement destructuring (record, list, tuple, nominal)
description:
Destructuring in MATCH is fully implemented (tag, record, list, nominal, or-patterns, wildcard, int/string/bool/char patterns). Typechecker and IR lowering handle all these.

**What's NOT implemented:**
- Let-binding destructuring: `let { name, age } = person` or `let [first, ..rest] = list`
- Assignment destructuring: `(x, y) = coords`

Currently let/assignment only supports simple identifiers as targets.
close_reason: Superseded by camp-x7w (let-binding destructuring) — match destructuring is already fully implemented.

title: Implement tuple types
description:
Implement tuple types.

**Syntax recipe decision:** `(T1, T2)` for tuple types, max 3 elements. Tuple construction and destructuring.

**Kitchen-sink:** Documented as comments only, no executable test code.

**Implementation scope:** Lexer (parenthesized comma-separated), parser (tuple type, tuple expression, tuple pattern), typechecker (tuple type with positional access), codegen (stack-allocated, positional field access).
close_reason: Duplicate of camp-wpi (tuple types and expressions).

title: Implement list literals with spread syntax
description:
List literals are IMPLEMENTED (parser, typechecker, IR lowering to Cons/Nil chains, codegen). Spread syntax `..spread` in list elements is NOT implemented.

**What's missing:**
- `..spread` in list literal expressions (e.g., `[1, ..rest, 3]`)
- `..rest` in list patterns (e.g., `[first, ..rest]`)

The `..` spread syntax exists for records, record patterns, tag unions, and effect rows — just not for list elements/patterns.
close_reason: Superseded by camp-i7j (list spread syntax) — basic list literals are already implemented.

title: Implement crash keyword
description:
Implement `crash` keyword.

**Syntax recipe decision:** `crash "message"` — immediate runtime trap with message. Unlike `todo` (placeholder for unfinished code), `crash` is intentional (e.g., unreachable branches).

**What exists:** `todo` keyword is implemented (produces `IR_Crash` with "todo: not implemented" message). `crash` would be similar but with user-provided message and different semantics (not expected to be replaced later).

**Implementation scope:** Lexer (`crash` keyword), parser (crash expression), typechecker (has type `a` / bottom), codegen (emit WASM trap with message).
close_reason: Already implemented. crash is a keyword (lexer.odin:33), Expr_Crash in AST (ast.odin:404-407), parser handles it (parser.odin:493-498).

title: Implement type aliases
description:
Implement type alias declarations.

**Syntax recipe decision:** `IntList : List(I64)`, `Coords : { x: F64, y: F64 }` — type aliases create named shorthand for types.

**Kitchen-sink:** Documented as comments only, no executable test code.

**Implementation scope:** Parser (type alias declaration), typechecker (expand alias during unification or track as named type), codegen (transparent — no runtime representation).
close_reason: Already implemented. Type aliases parsed as Decl_Alias (ast.odin:65-70) when Upper_Id : Type without = body (parser.odin:286-291).

title: Implement numeric literal syntax (hex, octal, binary, underscores, scientific)
description:
Numeric literal variants are PARTIALLY implemented. Underscore separators work (lexer.odin:311-313, char_class.odin:138-143).

**Still missing:**
- Hex: `0xFF` — no 0x prefix handling
- Octal: `0o77` — no 0o prefix handling
- Binary: `0b1010` — no 0b prefix handling
- Scientific: `1.0e10` — no e/E exponent notation
close_reason: Superseded by camp-8ss (hex/octal/binary/scientific numeric literals) — underscore separators already work.

title: Implement raw identifiers (backtick syntax)
description:
Implement raw identifier syntax (backtick).

**Syntax recipe decision:** `` `do` = 42 `` — backtick-wrapped identifiers allow using reserved words as identifiers.

**Kitchen-sink:** Documented as comments only, no executable test code.

**Implementation scope:** Lexer (backtick-delimited identifiers), parser (use as regular name), typechecker (treat as normal identifier).
close_reason: Already implemented. Backtick identifiers handled in lexer (lexer.odin:195-208), producing regular .Identifier tokens.

title: Implement dot lambdas (.field, .method())
description:
Implement dot lambda syntax (`.field`, `.method()`).

**Syntax recipe decisions:**
- `.field` — creates a lambda that accesses a field: `.name` ≡ `|r| r.name`
- `.method()` — creates a lambda that calls a method: `.length()` ≡ `|x| x.length()`
- `.->func()` — lexical UFCS in dot lambda form
- `.(field)()` — structural dispatch in dot lambda form

**Kitchen-sink:** Documented as comments only, no executable test code.

**Implementation scope:** Lexer (dot prefix), parser (dot lambda expression), typechecker (infer lambda type from context), codegen (generate closure).
close_reason: Already implemented. Dot lambdas parsed in parser_parse_dot_lambda (parser.odin:765-895) with .method(), .(field)(), .->func() variants.

title: Implement pointless evaluation diagnostic
description:
Implement pointless evaluation diagnostic.

**Current state:** `src/analysis/unused.odin:668` has `// TODO: implement pointless evaluation diagnostic`. The infrastructure partially exists (checks for `.Wildcard` classification) but the actual purity check is missing.

**E2e test affected:** unused-analysis/pointless-eval — test expects a `pointless_evaluation` diagnostic but it compiles without error.

**Spec reference:** `openspec/specs/unused-analysis/spec.md` — `_ = pureExpr` should warn.

title: Implement full LSP server
description:
LSP server is PARTIALLY implemented. Working: stdin/stdout transport, JSON-RPC, document sync (open/change/close/save), diagnostics publishing, go-to-definition (symbol index), hover (type signature).

**Still missing:**
- Completions
- Find references
- Signature help
- Code actions
- Workspace features
- Formatting via textDocument/formatting
close_reason: Too broad — LSP basics are implemented. Split into camp-m95 (remaining LSP features) which tracks the actual gaps.

title: Implement tree-sitter grammar for Camp
description:
Implement tree-sitter grammar for Camp.

**Spec'd but unimplemented (from tree-sitter/spec.md):**
- Full grammar covering all syntactic constructs
- External scanner for string interpolation brace-depth tracking
- Corpus tests for all constructs
- Syntax highlighting queries (`highlights.scm`)
- Scope/locals tracking (`locals.scm`)
- Symbol tagging (`tags.scm`)
- CI synchronization check (grammar matches parser)
- Per-line prefix multiline string parse tree
- Interpolation highlighting (delimiters as `@punctuation.special`)

**Spec reference:** `openspec/specs/tree-sitter/spec.md`
close_reason: Already implemented. 682-line grammar.js with external scanner, bindings for C/Rust/Go/Node/Python, highlight/fold/indent queries, test corpus.

title: Implement camp doc and doc comments (///)
description:
Implement `camp doc` HTML documentation generator.

**Spec'd but unimplemented (from doc-comments/spec.md):**
- `///` doc comment attachment to declarations
- `//#` hidden line processing in doc code blocks
- Module-level doc comments
- Markdown rendering in docs and LSP hover
- `camp doc` HTML documentation generation
- Doctest compilation and execution (also in testing-language/spec.md)

**Spec reference:** `openspec/specs/doc-comments/spec.md`
close_reason: camp doc is the only genuinely missing tooling feature. The doc comments (///) and //# hidden lines are not implemented in the compiler, and there's no HTML doc generator. However, this was too broad — the real gap is just the doc generator, not the entire doc comment system.

title: Implement camp.toml manifest and camp build command
description:
Implement `camp.toml` project manifest and `camp build` command.

**From syntax-recipe.md Section 14 (TBD items):**
- `camp.toml` format: project manifest for dependencies and metadata
- `camp build` CLI: build system command
- Shebang dependency syntax: single-file scripts need a way to declare deps without `camp.toml`

**Spec reference:** `openspec/specs/modules/spec.md` (project discovery, caching)
close_reason: camp build is implemented. camp.toml is genuinely missing but this bead conflated two things. The build command works; only the manifest format is missing.

title: Implement diagnostics rendering (multi-span, CLI snippets, --explain)
description:
Diagnostics rendering is PARTIALLY implemented. CLI rendering exists with ANSI color (auto TTY detection, NO_COLOR), source snippets with line numbers, primary ^ markers, secondary ~ labels, word-wrapped messages, hints, and error count summary (renderer_cli.odin). LSP rendering also implemented (renderer_lsp.odin). 1000+ diagnostic constructors.

**Still missing:**
- `--explain` flag for error code explanations
- Snapshot-deterministic output (80 char fixed wrap, no color for snapshots)
close_reason: Too broad — diagnostics rendering is mostly implemented. Split into camp-181 (--explain flag) which is the real gap.

title: Implement effect polymorphism and composition aliases
description:
Implement effect polymorphism and composition features.

**Spec'd but unimplemented (from effects/spec.md):**
- Effect polymorphism: row variables `e` propagated through function types
- Effect composition via aliases: `Io!: [File! | Console!]`
- Parameterized effects with tag union widening: `Throw!([NotFound | PermissionDenied])`
- Effect row subtraction: handle removes effect from row (partially implemented — e2e test exists)

**Spec reference:** `openspec/specs/effects/spec.md`
close_reason: Already implemented. Effect type params with is_effect flag (check_expr.odin:25-35), row variable marking (typecheck.odin:701-714), row unification with rest variable (unify.odin:306-399).

title: Implement module system (cross-module resolution, visibility, caching)
description:
Implement the remaining module system features beyond basic import syntax.

**Spec'd but unimplemented (from modules/spec.md):**
- Cross-module import resolution: qualified, selective, aliased, variant imports with `[Ok, Err]`
- Import conflict detection: local vs import, two imports of same name
- Cyclic dependency detection
- Visibility enforcement (`pub` / private) — `camp-xlw` was closed but full enforcement across modules TBD
- Unified namespace per module
- Prelude injection with compiler-injected types (partially via build/stdlib.odin)
- Prelude opt-out (`import Camp {}`)
- Per-file content hash caching (SHA256, `~/.cache/camp/`, dependency invalidation)
- Separate front-end, whole-program back-end (parallel parse/canonicalize/typecheck, then combined IR)
- Cross-module type compatibility (structural unification across modules)
- WASM name namespace collision handling (mangled `List__map` vs `Dict__map`)
- Runtime deduplication (emit `camp_alloc`, `camp_drop` etc exactly once)

**Spec reference:** `openspec/specs/modules/spec.md`
close_reason: Already implemented. Import resolution (import_resolve.odin), visibility enforcement, ambiguity detection, cyclic dep detection via topological sort (module_graph.odin), project discovery (discovery.odin).

title: Implement SIMD lexing for maximally performant lexing/parsing
close_reason: SIMD lexing fully implemented in lexer.odin and char_class.odin with SIMD paths for whitespace, identifiers, numbers, strings, per-line content. Extensive tests in test_lexer.odin.

title: Research FFI design for Camp
description:
Deep research into FFI design for a WASM/WASI-targeted language. Key questions:
- How should Camp call external WASI functions? 
- What safety boundaries are needed (no `unsafe` keyword for now, but FFI is inherently unsafe)?
- Prior art: Rust's FFI model, Zig's `@cImport`, WASI component model, etc.
- Should there be a separate FFI declaration syntax?
- How does this interact with Perceus reference counting (external code can't participate in RC)?
- Security model: trusted vs untrusted external code

This task blocks any FFI implementation work.

title: Parser: // line comments
description:
Parser only supports `--` comments. Doesn't support `//` single-line comments.

Blocks 1 e2e test: generic-list-map
close_reason: Already implemented: lexer handles // line comments in lexer_skip_whitespace (lexer.odin:73-81). Also /// doc comments handled separately.

Parser doesn't support match arms without leading `|` and pipe-separated:
- `match xs { Nil => Nil | Cons(h, t) => ... }`

Blocks 1 e2e test: generic-list-map (also blocked by // comments)
close_reason: Already implemented: parser supports | as match arm separator with optional leading | (parser.odin:1228-1276). Or-patterns also supported.

title: Break down the main src/ folder into packages where reasonable
Design and implement string interpolation support

close_reason: Already fully implemented: lexer handles ${expr} interpolation (lexer.odin:310), parser splits into String_Part segments (parser.odin:2148), canonicalizes (canonicalize.odin:633), typechecks with Display trait constraint (typecheck.odin:388), IR lowers to Str.concat + Display.to_str (lower.odin:1012). E2e tests passing. Spec exists at openspec/specs/string-interpolation/spec.md.

- acceptance: language/spec.md documents par syntax, method sugar, new prelude types/tags/effects

title: Update parallelism spec for any! return type and par_any! method
description:

- priority: 2

    Two discrepancies between spec and implementation:
    1. Spec says `any!` returns first successful `a`; implementation returns `List(a)` like `all!`
    2. `par_any!` method sugar exists in canonicalize but isn't in the spec
- acceptance: parallelism/spec.md matches implementation for any! return type and documents par_any! method sugar
close_reason: Already documented: parallelism spec defines any! return type (spec.md:37-41) and par_any! method sugar with desugaring details (spec.md:55-69).

title: Implement Iter stdlib module
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 2
- labels: stdlib
- description: |
    Iter(a) is declared in the prelude as a constructor with arity 1, but no stdlib/Iter.camp file exists. Iterators are needed for the sequential Parallel! handler.
- acceptance: Iter module with map/filter/fold/collect/for_each operations

description:

- labels: docs,packages

    The packages spec doesn't document the embedded stdlib modules (Result, Option, Bool, Int, Str, List) or the `stdlib_lookup`/`register_stdlib_modules` discovery fallback mechanism.
- acceptance: packages/spec.md documents embedded stdlib modules and discovery fallback
# Compiler Gaps

title: Add CAMP_THREADS env var and CPU detection fallbacks
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 2
- labels: cli,config,parallelism
- description: |
    The parallelism spec says thread count priority should be: CLI flag > CAMP_THREADS env var > CPU detection. Currently only the `--threads` CLI flag is parsed. The `CAMP_THREADS` env var and `num_cpus()` detection are missing.
- acceptance: CAMP_THREADS env var works; defaults to CPU count when neither flag nor env is set
# Language Feature Gaps

title: Implement for loop syntax
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 2
- labels: parser,canonicalize
- description: |
    `Kw_For` exists in the token enum but there's no `for x in xs { body }` parsing. The `par for` variant works but plain `for` doesn't.
- design: |
    1. Parse `for x in xs { body }` in parser_parse_prefix
    2. Desugar to `xs.iter().for_each(|x| body)` or equivalent recursive function
- acceptance: `for x in xs { body }` parses and desugars correctly
close_reason: Already implemented end-to-end: for x in xs { body } parses (parser.odin:454-465), canonicalizes (canonicalize.odin:737-742), typechecks (typecheck.odin:633-659), lowers to IR_Loop (lower.odin:278-289), and codegens to Wasm block/loop (emit_expr.odin:248-292). Implementation uses direct linked-list iteration rather than desugaring to for_each, but the feature is functionally complete.

title: Implement no-shadowing enforcement
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 3
- labels: typecheck
- description: |
    The language spec requires no-shadowing enforcement — a variable cannot shadow another in the same scope. Not implemented.
- acceptance: Compiler errors on variable shadowing
close_reason: Already implemented: check_shadow in typecheck.odin:46-51 is called at all binding sites (const, let, lambda params, match arms, for-vars, mutable vars). diag_shadow diagnostic exists.

title: Implement atomic WASM opcodes in codegen
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 2
- labels: codegen,parallelism
- description: |
    All six atomic IR nodes (IR_Atomic_Load, IR_Atomic_Store, IR_Atomic_RMW, IR_Atomic_Fence, IR_Wait, IR_Notify) emit Wasm_Unreachable in codegen. The actual WASM atomic opcodes (0xFE prefix) need to be emitted.
- design: |
    Per openspec/specs/parallelism/design.md §WASM Threads:
    1. IR_Atomic_Load{.B4}: emit 0xFE 0x10 + alignment + offset
    2. IR_Atomic_Store{.B4}: emit 0xFE 0x17 + alignment + offset
    3. IR_Atomic_RMW{.Add, .B4}: emit 0xFE 0x1E + alignment + offset
    4. IR_Atomic_RMW{.CmpXchg, .B4}: emit 0xFE 0x48 + alignment + offset
    5. IR_Atomic_Fence: emit 0xFE 0x50
    6. IR_Wait{.B4}: emit 0xFE 0x52 + alignment + offset
    7. IR_Notify: emit 0xFE 0x54 + alignment + offset
- acceptance: Atomic ops compile to correct WASM bytecode; shared memory programs work
close_reason: Atomic WASM opcodes fully implemented: IR_Atomic_Load/Store/RMW/Fence defined in ir.odin, handled through full pipeline, emitted in emit_expr.odin with Wasm_Atomic_Mem instructions.

title: Update compiler design for codegen status and runtime count
description:
- type: chore
- priority: 2
- labels: docs,compiler
- description: |
    The compiler design (openspec/specs/compiler/design.md) codegen status table is outdated. IR_I32_Load, IR_I32_Store, IR_Closure_Call, IR_Resume now have working codegen. IR_Method_Call, IR_Handle, IR_Perform still emit Unreachable (by design — lowered away by effect_lower). Runtime function count is now 17 (was 6). Atomic IR nodes exist but emit Unreachable. camp_worker_entry export exists.
- acceptance: compiler/design.md codegen table reflects current implementation status

title: Implement Map stdlib module
description:
- type: feature

- labels: stdlib

    Map(k,v) is declared in the prelude as a constructor with arity 2, but no stdlib/Map.camp file exists and no runtime functions for hash maps are implemented.
- acceptance: Map module with insert/lookup/delete/keys/values operations

title: Implement remaining effect stdlib modules (File!, Env!, Time!, Random!)
description:
Implement the remaining effect stdlib modules: File!, Env!, Time!, Random!.

**Known gaps:**
- `readln!` Console operation: handler emits `unreachable` at runtime (emit_expr.odin:1667) — traps instead of reading input
- I/O bridge deferred: File!/Console read operations use placeholder pollable `0` (emit_expr.odin:1060-1071, comment: "Full implementation deferred to I/O bridge (Group 6)")
- `Time.sleep!` passes hard-coded `0` for task_ptr because scheduler context isn't wired through (emit_expr.odin:1054-1056)

**E2e tests affected:** Several string interpolation and pattern matching tests compile but fail at WASM runtime with "Not_Exist" due to missing I/O runtime support.

title: Update parallelism design for CLI flags and worker entry
description:
- type: chore
- priority: 2
- labels: docs,parallelism
- description: |
    The parallelism design doesn't document: `--threads` CLI flag, `CAMP_THREADS` config variable, `camp_worker_entry` WASM export, or atomic IR nodes. These are all now implemented.
- acceptance: parallelism/design.md documents --threads, CAMP_THREADS, camp_worker_entry, and atomic IR nodes

title: Update effects spec with Parallel/Spawn/Async prelude effects
description:
- type: chore
- priority: 2
- labels: docs,effects
- description: |
    The effects spec (openspec/specs/effects/spec.md) doesn't document Parallel!, Spawn!, or Async! as prelude effects. These are now injected in `inject_prelude` with full operation signatures. The spec needs updating to reflect the current prelude.
- acceptance: effects/spec.md documents all five prelude effects (Console!, Throw!, Parallel!, Spawn!, Async!) with their operations

title: Update effects design for 4-byte evidence slots
description:
- type: chore
- priority: 2
- labels: docs,effects
- description: |
    The effects design (openspec/specs/effects/design.md) specifies 8-byte evidence record slots (fn_idx + env_ptr). The implementation uses 4-byte slots storing a closure pointer directly, then loading fn_idx and env from within the closure at dispatch time. The design doc should reflect this optimization.
- acceptance: effects/design.md documents 4-byte evidence slots with closure pointer layout

title: Implement Set stdlib module
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 2
- labels: stdlib
- description: |
    Set(a) is declared in the prelude as a constructor with arity 1, but no stdlib/Set.camp file exists.
- acceptance: Set module with insert/contains/remove/union/intersection operations

title: Implement $ mutable variable semantics
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 2
- labels: parser,typecheck,codegen
- description: |
    `$`-prefixed variables are parsed but no mutation semantics are enforced. The spec says `$` variables can be reassigned within their scope but cannot be captured by closures (especially parallel closures).
- acceptance: $ variables can be reassigned; compiler prevents capture by closures

title: Structured concurrency warnings for unjoined spawns
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 2
- labels: typecheck,parallelism
- description: |
    The parallelism spec requires that every `Spawn.spawn!` must be followed by exactly one `Spawn.join!` or `Spawn.cancel!` before the handler exits. Currently there's no enforcement — unjoined spawns silently leak resources.
- design: |
    1. In typecheck, track spawned handles in a set within the handler scope
    2. On handler exit, check if any handles are unjoined
    3. Emit warning (future: error) for unjoined spawns
    4. Handler auto-cancels outstanding handles on exit
- acceptance: Compiler warns when a spawned handle is never joined or cancelled

title: Implement trait stdlib modules (Eq, Ord, Hash, Display, Clone)
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 2
- labels: stdlib,generics-traits
- description: |
    Core traits (Eq, Ord, Hash, Display, Clone) are specified but not implemented. These are needed for Map/Set keys, formatting, and comparison.
- acceptance: Eq/Ord/Hash/Display/Clone traits defined with implementations for primitive types

title: Handle(a) opacity and one-shot enforcement
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 2
- labels: typecheck,codegen,parallelism
- description: |
    Handle(a) is specified as opaque, one-shot, and move-semantics only. Currently it's just `i32` with no encapsulation. No runtime error on double-join. Cannot be passed to another spawned computation.
- design: |
    1. Type-level: Handle(a) should be a distinct type, not just i32
    2. Runtime: track handle state (Pending/Completed/Joined/Cancelled) in a handle table
    3. Double-join or double-cancel should trap
    4. Move semantics: after join/cancel, handle variable is consumed
- acceptance: Double-join traps at runtime; Handle cannot be used after consumption
# Runtime Gaps

title: Enforce pub visibility during import resolution
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 2
- labels: typecheck,import_resolve
- description: |
    `Kw_Pub` is parsed but not enforced during import resolution. All names are currently accessible regardless of pub annotation.
- acceptance: Non-pub names are not accessible from other modules
close_reason: Already implemented: export_table.odin only includes is_pub items, import_resolve.odin checks is_pub for named imports and qualified access, project.odin filters cross-module types by is_pub.

title: Implement camp test / camp fmt / camp check commands
description:
camp build/test/check CLI is IMPLEMENTED. 5 commands: Build, Test, Check, Fmt, Lsp. camp build does full compilation to .wasm. camp test finds test/expect decls, compiles each as main!, runs via wasmtime. camp check does parse+typecheck only.

**Still missing:**
- Parallel test execution with runtime.cpu_count() workers
